answer: A beacon-anchored liveness check makes each identity earn its keep: every epoch a public beacon emits an unpredictable task, and an agent must return a verifiable result within a short window. Results accumulate in an open atlas of past work, so reputation follows a continuous pulse of completed tasks, not a claimed name. An attacker spinning up thousands of sock puppets must pay real compute for every identity in every round, while an honest agent pays only once. Copied or precomputed answers fail because the beacon value cannot be known in advance.
